findings.issue: A1 is genuinely absent from SEAT_PROTOCOL. MODEL_MATRIX contains only the narrower Sol-specific instruction to run reviews in the background; it does not require harness tracking or forbid raw detachment. The proposed universal rule is nevertheless overfitted to Claude: Codex is unverified, and a supervised host process that emits durable completion can detach safely while a harness-tracked process can still fail before publishing durable evidence.
findings.suggestion: Put the runtime-neutral invariant in SEAT_PROTOCOL: actionable asynchronous work must be supervised and must produce a durable terminal outcome. Put exact Claude launch mechanics, empirical notification tables, and Codex probes in MODEL_MATRIX or runtime-adapter conformance. Forbid unsupervised `nohup … &`, not detachment as a category.

findings.section: A2 — tool completions as hub events
findings.issue: The obligation is genuinely absent. SEAT_PROTOCOL mentions mailbox/artifact events and subagent task records, but not durable review-tool completion. HUB_DATA_MODEL supplies generic atomic event semantics yet has no completion entity or verb. Therefore A2's “completion via hub append” lacks a normative event type, payload, recipient, and multi-recipient atomicity contract. B6's “mail invoking seat + o” could become two separately failing sends and duplicates when o is the invoker.
findings.suggestion: Make HUB_DATA_MODEL the normative owner of a generic completion verb/event carrying hub_id, run/correlation id, terminal outcome including failure/cancellation, result reference or digest, optional verdict/schema validity, originating dispatch, producer, and deduplicated recipients. One event should project to all recipients atomically. SEAT_PROTOCOL should only require actionable completions to use that event and treat it as a doorbell source.

findings.issue: A3 is genuinely absent, but it contradicts the existing standby liveness predicate. It deliberately suppresses rings for info/status while still allowing those messages to age as oldest undrained mail; normal policy-driven deferral will therefore classify a healthy seat as STALLED after mail_grace. “Next wake” is undefined for a standby seat, which has no ordinary scheduled wake under §2.
findings.suggestion: Define a bounded deferred ring with max_deferral strictly below mail_grace, or make the liveness predicate class-aware and add a separate delivery-age SLO for filtered traffic. Unknown or malformed classes must ring by default. SEAT_PROTOCOL owns interrupt/defer behavior, HUB_DATA_MODEL owns the canonical class taxonomy, and MODEL_MATRIX owns per-seat mappings and thresholds.

findings.issue: The location enum is genuinely new, although §1 already says watcher state belongs to seat control and §4 already requires the pacemaker to read it. Merely recording an in-session watcher's existence and generation does not make its death externally observable: a dead watcher leaves the same record behind. The draft also conflates supported capability, selected topology, and live watcher state in one field.
findings.suggestion: Keep A4 in SEAT_PROTOCOL but separate `capabilities.watcher_locations` from live `watcher` state. The latter needs location, generation, target session handle, status, last-observed/last-poll time, and expiry or another externally testable health signal. An in-session watcher is conforming only while that signal is renewed outside the seat heartbeat contract.

findings.issue: B1 cannot be repaired in isolation. Current `msg.sh send` writes recipient JSONL directly without hub_id, while `msg.sh hub` also writes the mailbox first and relies on a later ingester to create hub state. That violates HUB_DATA_MODEL §1's authoritative hub append plus derived outbox projection and permits transport/record split. Plain messages also cannot satisfy B1's idempotent-by-hub_id processing rule. A2 cannot honestly ship through this path as a “hub event.”
findings.suggestion: Add a prerequisite conformance gap for replacing sender-written mailbox files with an authoritative hub append/outbox path, migrating plain sends to identified events, and implementing sender read-back/digest verification. Only then add processing cursors and completion events.

findings.section: B3 — watchdog grounding and deployment conformance
findings.issue: B3 contains one false claim and omits two material gaps. Both the live watchdog and newer repo mirror already emit a sweep-completion line. However, the main checkout has no watchdog file, the live host copy and newer mirror differ, and both enumerate a hardcoded roster. Those violate §4's versioned-in-repo and registry-enumerated requirements. Also, cadence_seconds=0 is not itself the standby defect; the missing independent canary/floor branch is.
findings.suggestion: Correct B3 before attachment: retain PID-skip, missing canary/floor, and predicate defects; remove the completion-line claim; add hardcoded-roster and live-versus-versioned deployment drift. Require one deployable source with provenance and an explicit propagation/read-back check.

findings.section: B5/B6 — cross-source coalescing and watcher fixtures
findings.issue: The prior dual-signal finding is not fully dispositioned. Existing §4 coalescing governs doorbell bursts, not necessarily the race between a harness task-exit notification and A2's completion event. Depending on ordering, the invoking seat can receive two turns even when processing is idempotent. B5 also does not explicitly require dynamic stream discovery, per-seat rather than per-file quiet-window behavior, or generation supersession tests.
findings.suggestion: Use run_id correlation across task notification and hub completion, suppress a doorbell poke when the processing cursor already covers the completion, and deduplicate the o-as-invoker recipient case. Add deterministic fixtures for both signal orderings, new sender-file discovery, to-all delivery, many sender files yielding one wake, watcher restart/generation supersession, and unknown message classes.

findings.issue: The rollout shape and metrics are substantially improved, but it still lacks go/no-go thresholds. Shadow mode has a duration but no minimum eligible events per class; the live pilot has neither duration nor sample floor. “Hundreds” is not a declared confidence target. The abbreviated offline fixture list omits several mandatory §2 lease cases, transport partial-write recovery, filter-induced false stalls, watcher restart, and dual-signal races. Shadowing also cannot validate actual invocation recovery.
findings.suggestion: Make all relevant B-items prerequisites to shadow mode. Run the complete normative conformance suites, not only the four examples. Define per-class sample floors and explicit SLOs for p95/max latency, zero lost processing, duplicate-wake ceiling, watcher death-detection bound, false-stall ceiling, fallback-rescue ceiling, and normalized token cost. During the live pilot inject watcher, session, and pacemaker death/restart, then expand fleet in staged cohorts with rollback triggers.

strongest_aspect: The structural disposition is correct: r1 was withdrawn, the stronger existing cursor/lease/canary/coalescing contract is now authoritative, and Part C sensibly moves conformance and shadow observation ahead of live invocation.
biggest_risk: A3 currently turns intentional filtering into a false stall, while A2 assumes an atomic hub completion path that neither the hub verb model nor the live mailbox-first implementation yet provides.
